prose:
The eval asked for a fix to src/duration.ts so that parse_duration never returns a
negative value for input like "-3s". The agent read tests/duration.test.js first, then
opened src/duration.ts and found parse_duration propagating the sign of the input at
lines 22-27. It applied one hunk clamping negative durations to zero and re-ran the
suite; all three verifier checks pass. Kratos and logos both located the sign-propagation
site, citing the same range, so the defect counts as one observation. The patch contains
no unrelated edits.

The reward of 1 follows from all three verifier checks passing after the clamp hunk;
the assembled record supports it byte-for-byte.

Two committed rounds; each improvement carries one resolving ref and the corroborated
defect rests on a single ref counted once, so high confidence is not claimed here.
Read the failing test before opening the implementation.
Confined the fix to a single clamping hunk in parse_duration.
No comment near the clamp explains why negative inputs are legal but coerced.
Consider reviewing src/duration.ts before the next run, and re-running tests/duration.test.js to confirm current behaviour.
The repository also contains a README whose accuracy was not assessed this round.
A maintainer may wish to open README.md at some point ahead of a future evaluation to see whether it still reads accurately.
Broader familiarity with the module could conceivably be beneficial.
